slides.stem:
How many real solutions does the equation

$\frac{3}{x - 2} + \frac{4}{x + 2} = \frac{14}{x^2 - 4}$

have?

slides.intro: Clear the denominators, then count what survives.
slides.trapWhy: Zero throws away $x = \frac{16}{7}$ as "extraneous". It breaks no denominator, so it counts.
slides.stem: How many real solutions does the equation have?

slides.title: Extraneous means breaks a denominator
slides.body:
Multiply by the LCD, solve, then test each root against the original denominators. Discard only the roots that hit zero down there.

$x = \frac{16}{7}$ makes every denominator perfectly fine, so it stays.

slides.title: When you miss one like this, Seva tells you why.
